summary.text: Bobby Pulido is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Monica De La Cruz in Texas's 15th District. An Edinburg native, he has been a Tejano recording artist for about three decades and describes himself as a small-business owner and father of four. He is running on affordability, water infrastructure, public education and comprehensive immigration reform, and won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Ada Cuellar.

paragraphs.text: Pulido was born in Edinburg, Texas, in 1973, the oldest child of Tejano singer Roberto Pulido, and graduated from Edinburg High School.
He was accepted at St. Mary's University, where he studied political science, before leaving college to pursue a singing career.
He debuted with his own band in 1995 and signed with EMI Latin; his debut album Desvelado was certified platinum by the RIAA.

The Texas Tribune describes him as known for 1990s hits including "Desvelado" and "Se Murió de Amor", a five-time Latin Grammy nominee and 22-time Tejano Music Award nominee who won eight times early in his career.
He has also acted, including a lead role in the 2003 television film La Decada Furiosa.
According to his campaign website, he has run businesses and created jobs in South Texas; Ballotpedia lists his career as musician and small business owner.
He announced a run for Congress in September 2025, after forming an exploratory committee that July, to challenge De La Cruz.
Pulido won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Ada Cuellar with 67.5% of the vote.
According to his campaign website, he is a father of four.

sources.title: Tejano star Bobby Pulido launches South Texas congressional run
